translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Cixi was interred, he served as Commissioner entering the underground palace with the coffin, reverently checked the spirit tablet, and was advanced to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the interment of Empress Dowager Cixi he entered the underground palace with the coffin, reverently verified the spirit tablet, and was promoted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 三年，裁禮部，改為弼德院副院長。

translations.literal: In the third year the Ministry of Rites was abolished and he was made Vice President of the Institute for Royal Tutors.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when the Ministry of Rites was abolished, he became Vice President of the Institute for Royal Tutors.

sentences.zh: 旋充顧問大臣、德宗實錄館總裁。

translations.literal: Soon after he served as Advisory Minister and Director-General of the Veritable Records of the Guangxu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served as Advisory Minister and Director-General of the Guangxu Emperor's Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 國變後，避居天津。

translations.literal: After the change of dynasty he withdrew to Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the dynasty he retired to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十八，諡文恪。

translations.literal: He died at fifty-eight; his posthumous title was Wenge.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-eight and was posthumously titled Wenge (Cultivated and Reverent).

sentences.zh: 榮慶持躬謹慎。

translations.literal: Rong Qing conducted himself with caution and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Qing was scrupulous and self-restrained in his conduct.

sentences.zh: 故事，軍機大臣無公費，率取給餽贐。

translations.literal: By precedent Grand Councilors had no public stipend and generally drew their support from gifts.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent Grand Councilors received no public stipend and generally lived on gifts from petitioners.

sentences.zh: 榮慶始入直，深以為病，語同列合辭上請，乃得支養廉銀二千，而御前諸臣亦援例增給有差。

translations.literal: When Rong Qing first entered duty he took this deeply as a fault; he spoke with his colleagues and they jointly memorialized, whereupon they received two thousand taels of integrity-nourishing silver, and the officials before the throne also received increased allotments by precedent in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong Qing first entered the Council he regarded this practice as deeply corrupt; he persuaded his colleagues to petition jointly, securing two thousand taels of integrity stipend, and officials at court also received increased allotments by precedent in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 那桐，字琴軒，葉赫那拉氏，內務府滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Na Tong, styled Qinxuan, of the Yehe Nara clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner under the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: Na Tong, styled Qinxuan, of the Yehe Nara clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner attached to the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 光緒十一年舉人，由戶部主事歷保四品京堂，授鴻臚寺卿，遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Guangxu he became a provincial graduate; from a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue he rose through successive promotions to fourth-rank capital official, was appointed Director of Banquets, and was transferred to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate of Guangxu 11, he rose from a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue through successive promotions to fourth-rank capital official, became Director of Banquets, and was appointed Grand Secretariat Academician.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，兼直總理各國事務衙門，晉理籓院侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he concurrently served in the Office for Managing Affairs of All Nations and was advanced to Vice Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 26 he served concurrently in the Zongli Yamen and was promoted Vice Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 拳匪肇釁，各國聯兵來犯，令赴丰台御之。

translations.literal: When the Boxer rebels provoked trouble and allied armies of the powers invaded, he was ordered to Fengtai to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxers provoked conflict and allied foreign armies invaded, he was ordered to Fengtai to meet them.

sentences.zh: 外兵入京，誤以東壩為匪窟，欲屠之，力解乃免。

translations.literal: When foreign troops entered the capital they mistook Dongba for a rebel nest and intended to massacre it; he argued forcefully and secured its escape.
translations.idiomatic: When foreign troops entered Beijing they mistook Dongba for a rebel stronghold and planned a massacre; he argued forcefully and saved the district.

sentences.zh: 兩宮西巡，命充留京辦事大臣，隨李鴻章議和。

translations.literal: When the two palaces toured west, he was ordered to serve as Commissioner remaining in the capital and joined Li Hongzhang in negotiating peace.
translations.idiomatic: When the court fled west, he was appointed Commissioner in Beijing and joined Li Hongzhang in peace negotiations.

sentences.zh: 約成，專使日本謝罪，又派赴日觀博覽會。

translations.literal: When the treaty was concluded he went as special envoy to Japan to offer apology and was again dispatched to Japan to attend the exposition.
translations.idiomatic: After the treaty was signed he went to Japan as special envoy to offer apology, and was later sent again to attend the exposition in Japan.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，擢戶部尚書，調外務部，兼步​​軍統領，管工巡局事，創警務，繕路政。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was elevated to Minister of Revenue, transferred to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and concurrently served as Commander of the Metropolitan Garrison, overseeing the Works and Patrol Bureau, founding police administration, and repairing roads.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 29 he became Minister of Revenue, then Minister of Foreign Affairs, and concurrently Commander of the Metropolitan Garrison; he oversaw the Works and Patrol Bureau, established the police force, and improved road administration.

sentences.zh: 平反王維勤冤獄，商民頌之。

translations.literal: He reversed the wrongful case of Wang Weiqin, and merchants praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He reversed the wrongful conviction of Wang Weiqin, winning praise from merchants and townspeople.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，晉大學士，仍充外務部會辦大臣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was advanced to Grand Secretary and still served as Associate Minister of Foreign Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was promoted Grand Secretary while continuing as Associate Minister of Foreign Affairs.

sentences.zh: 歷兼釐訂官制、參預政務、變通旗制，署民政部尚書。

translations.literal: He successively served in revising the administrative system, participating in government affairs, and reforming the banner system, and acted as Minister of Civil Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served on commissions for administrative reform, government affairs, and banner reform, and acted as Minister of Civil Affairs.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，命為軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong he was appointed Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 1 he was appointed Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，請終制，不許。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother and requested full observance of mourning; permission was denied.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his mother's death he requested full mourning leave; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 出署直隸總督，請撥部款修鳳河。

translations.literal: He went out to act as Governor-General of Zhili and requested ministry funds to repair the Feng River.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting Governor-General of Zhili and requested ministry funds to repair the Feng River.

sentences.zh: 尋還直。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 三年，改官制，授內閣協理大臣，旋辭，充弼德院顧問大臣。

translations.literal: In the third year, when the administrative system was changed, he was appointed Associate Prime Minister of the Cabinet, soon resigned, and served as Advisory Minister of the Institute for Royal Tutors.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, under the new administrative system, he was appointed Associate Prime Minister of the Cabinet but soon resigned and became Advisory Minister of the Institute for Royal Tutors.

sentences.zh: 國變後，久臥病。

translations.literal: After the change of dynasty he lay long ill.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the dynasty he remained bedridden with illness for a long time.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十有九。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 戴鴻慈，字少懷，廣東南海人。

translations.literal: Dai Hongci, styled Shaohuai, a native of Nanhai, Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Hongci, styled Shaohuai, was a native of Nanhai in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年進士，改庶吉士，以編修督學山東。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the second year of Guangxu, he entered the Hanlin Academy as a probationer and, as Compiler, served as education commissioner for Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Guangxu 2, he entered the Hanlin Academy and, as Compiler, served as Shandong education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸，服除，督學雲南。

translations.literal: He returned on his father's death, and after mourning was completed served as education commissioner for Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home upon his father's death; after mourning he served as Yunnan education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 後復充雲南鄉試正考官。

translations.literal: Later he again served as chief examiner for the Yunnan provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He later served again as chief examiner for the Yunnan provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 二十年，大考一等，擢庶子。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he ranked first class in the great examination and was elevated to Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 20 he ranked first class in the palace examination and was promoted Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 日韓啟釁，我軍屢挫。

translations.literal: Japan and Korea provoked conflict and our armies suffered repeated defeats.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out between Japan and Korea, Qing forces suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 鴻慈連疏劾李鴻章調遣乖方，遷延貽誤，始終倚任丁汝昌，請予嚴懲；

translations.literal: Hongci repeatedly memorialized impeaching Li Hongzhang for perverse deployment, delay causing harm, and constant reliance on Ding Ruchang, requesting severe punishment;
translations.idiomatic: Hongci repeatedly impeached Li Hongzhang for mishandling deployments, fatal delays, and persistent reliance on Ding Ruchang, demanding severe punishment;

sentences.zh: 並責令速解汝昌到部治罪，以肅軍紀：均不報。

translations.literal: he also ordered that Ruchang be swiftly brought to the ministry for punishment to restore military discipline—all went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: and demanded that Ding Ruchang be swiftly brought to the ministry for trial to restore military discipline—all without response.

sentences.zh: 和議成，鴻慈奏善後十二策：一，審敵情以固邦交；

translations.literal: When the peace settlement was concluded Hongci memorialized twelve policies for recovery: first, examine enemy conditions to strengthen interstate relations;
translations.idiomatic: After the peace settlement Hongci submitted twelve recovery policies: first, assess enemy intentions to secure foreign relations;

sentences.zh: 二，增陪都以資拱衛；

translations.literal: second, increase the number of subsidiary capitals to provide protective encirclement;
translations.idiomatic: second, establish additional subsidiary capitals to strengthen the capital's defenses;

sentences.zh: 三，設軍屯以實邊儲；

translations.literal: third, establish military colonies to fill frontier stores;
translations.idiomatic: third, establish military colonies to build frontier grain reserves;

sentences.zh: 四，築鐵道以省漕運；

translations.literal: fourth, build railways to economize on grain transport;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, build railways to reduce reliance on the grain transport system;

sentences.zh: 五，開煤鐵以收利權；

translations.literal: fifth, open coal and iron mines to recover profit rights;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, develop coal and iron mining to retain economic sovereignty;

sentences.zh: 六，稅菸酒以佐度支；

translations.literal: sixth, tax tobacco and wine to assist state expenditure;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, levy taxes on tobacco and wine to supplement state revenue;

sentences.zh: 七，行抽練以簡軍實；

translations.literal: seventh, carry out selective drilling to streamline military substance;
translations.idiomatic: seventh, conduct selective training to streamline effective fighting forces;

sentences.zh: 八，廣鑄造以精器械；

translations.literal: eighth, broadly expand casting and manufacture to refine weapons;
translations.idiomatic: eighth, expand arms manufacture to improve weaponry;

sentences.zh: 九，簡使才以備折衝；

translations.literal: ninth, select diplomatic talent to prepare for negotiation;
translations.idiomatic: ninth, select capable diplomats for foreign negotiations;

sentences.zh: 十，重牧令以資治理；

translations.literal: tenth, value magistrates to supply governance;
translations.idiomatic: tenth, elevate county magistrates to strengthen local governance;

sentences.zh: 十一，召對群僚以勵交修；

translations.literal: eleventh, summon audiences with the assembled officials to encourage mutual improvement;
translations.idiomatic: eleventh, hold audiences with officials to encourage mutual counsel and improvement;

sentences.zh: 十二，變通考試以求實用。

translations.literal: twelfth, change and adapt examinations to seek practical utility.
translations.idiomatic: twelfth, reform the examination system to emphasize practical learning.

sentences.zh: 遷侍講學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 督學福建，再遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He served as education commissioner for Fujian and was again transferred to Grand Secretariat Academician.
translations.idiomatic: As Fujian education commissioner he was later promoted Grand Secretariat Academician.

sentences.zh: 學政報滿，假歸省墓。

translations.literal: When his term as education commissioner ended he took leave to return and visit the tombs.
translations.idiomatic: When his term as education commissioner ended he took leave to return home and tend the family graves.

sentences.zh: 擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was elevated to Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 赴西安行在，上陳治本疏；

translations.literal: He went to the traveling palace at Xi'an and submitted a memorial on fundamental remedies;
translations.idiomatic: He went to the court at Xi'an and submitted a memorial on fundamental reform;

sentences.zh: 又請建兩都，分六鎮，以總督兼經略大臣，得闢幕僚，巡撫以下咸受節制。

translations.literal: he also asked to establish two capitals, divide six garrisons, appoint governors-general concurrently as frontier commissioners with authority to recruit staff, and place all officials below governor below their command.
translations.idiomatic: he also proposed dual capitals, six military districts under governors-general serving concurrently as frontier commissioners with authority to recruit staff, with all officials below governor under their command.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，隨扈還京，轉戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: That winter he followed the entourage back to the capital and was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he returned to Beijing with the court and was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時各省教案滋多，鴻慈請設宣諭化導使，以學政兼充。

translations.literal: At the time missionary cases multiplied in the provinces; Hongci asked to establish Commissioners for Proclamation and Guidance, to be filled concurrently by education commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: As missionary incidents multiplied across the provinces, Hongci proposed Commissioners for Proclamation and Guidance, to be filled concurrently by education commissioners.

sentences.zh: 編輯外交成案，頒發宣講。

translations.literal: He compiled precedents in foreign affairs and issued them for proclamation and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled precedents in foreign affairs and distributed them for public instruction.

sentences.zh: 又請就翰林院創立報局，各省遵設官報，議格不行。

translations.literal: He also asked to establish a press bureau at the Hanlin Academy and have the provinces follow with official gazettes; the proposal was blocked and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed establishing a press bureau at the Hanlin Academy with official gazettes in each province; the proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 時設會議政務處，有奉旨交議事件，三品京堂以上與議。

translations.literal: At the time the Office for Deliberating Government Affairs was established; matters referred by imperial edict for deliberation were discussed by capital officials of third rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: The Office for Deliberating Government Affairs had been established; matters referred by imperial edict were discussed by capital officials of third rank and above.

sentences.zh: 鴻慈請推行閣部、九卿、翰林、科道皆得各抒所見，屬官則呈堂代遞，可以收群策、勵人才。

translations.literal: Hongci asked that ministries, the Nine Chief Ministers, Hanlin, and the censorate all be enabled to express their views; subordinates would present them through their superiors, thereby gathering collective counsel and encouraging talent.
translations.idiomatic: Hongci proposed that ministries, the Nine Chief Ministers, Hanlin, and the censorate all submit their views, with subordinates forwarding memorials through their superiors, to gather collective counsel and encourage talent.

sentences.zh: 下政務處採擇。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Office of Government Affairs for selection.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was referred to the Office of Government Affairs for consideration.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，命五大臣出使各國考求政治，鴻慈與焉。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year five great ministers were ordered to travel to various states to investigate government; Hongci was among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year five senior ministers were dispatched abroad to study foreign governments; Hongci was among them.

sentences.zh: 將發，黨人挾炸藥登車狙擊，從者或被創，人情惶懼。

translations.literal: As they were about to depart, party members boarded with explosives to ambush them; attendants were wounded and public feeling was fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Just before departure, revolutionaries boarded their train with explosives; attendants were wounded and panic spread.

sentences.zh: 鴻慈從容詣宮門取進止，兩宮慰諭，至泣下，遂行。

translations.literal: Hongci calmly went to the palace gate to seek instructions; the two palaces comforted and instructed him until they wept, and then he departed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongci calmly went to the palace for instructions; the Empress Dowager and Emperor comforted him until they wept, and he then departed.

sentences.zh: 歷十五邦，凡八閱月，歸國。

translations.literal: He visited fifteen states over eight months and returned to the country.
translations.idiomatic: He visited fifteen countries over eight months and returned home.

sentences.zh: 與載澤、端方、尚其亨、李盛鐸等裒輯列國政要百三十三卷、歐美政治要義十八章，會同進呈。

translations.literal: Together with Zai Ze, Duan Fang, Shang Qiheng, Li Shengduo, and others he compiled one hundred thirty-three fascicles of Essentials of Government among the Various States and eighteen chapters on Essentials of European and American Politics, and jointly presented them for imperial review.
translations.idiomatic: With Zai Ze, Duan Fang, Shang Qiheng, Li Shengduo, and others he compiled 133 volumes of Essentials of Government among the Nations and eighteen chapters on Western political essentials, and jointly submitted them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 並奏言：「各國治理大略，以為觀其政體：美為合眾，而專重民權；

translations.literal: They also memorialized, saying: "The broad outlines of how the various states are governed, viewed so as to observe their forms of polity: the United States is a union of peoples, yet lays especial weight on popular rights;
translations.idiomatic: They also submitted a memorial stating: "Surveying how nations govern, one may read their political forms: America is a federal republic that nevertheless places supreme emphasis on popular rights;

sentences.zh: 德本聯邦，而實為​​君主；

translations.literal: Germany is fundamentally a federation, yet is in fact a monarchy;
translations.idiomatic: Germany is nominally a federation but in practice a monarchy;

sentences.zh: 奧、匈同盟，仍各用其制度；

translations.literal: Austria and Hungary are allied, yet each still employs its own system;
translations.idiomatic: Austria and Hungary are united under one crown yet retain separate institutions;

sentences.zh: 法、義同族，不免偏於集權；

translations.literal: France and Italy are of the same race, and cannot but lean toward centralized power;
translations.idiomatic: France and Italy share a common Latin heritage and inevitably incline toward centralized authority;

sentences.zh: 唯英人循秩序而不好激進，其憲法出於自然之發達，行之百年而無弊。

translations.literal: Only the English follow order and do not love radicalism; their constitution arose from natural development and has been practiced for a century without defect.
translations.idiomatic: Only Britain cherishes order and shuns radical upheaval; its constitution grew by gradual evolution and has operated for a century without serious flaw.

sentences.zh: 反乎此者，有憲法不聯合之國，如瑞典、挪威則分離矣；

translations.literal: Contrary to this, there are states with constitutions but no union, as Sweden and Norway, which separated;
translations.idiomatic: By contrast, states with constitutions but no true union, such as Sweden and Norway, have split apart;

sentences.zh: 有憲法不完全之國，如土耳其、埃及則衰弱矣；

translations.literal: there are states with incomplete constitutions, as Turkey and Egypt, which grew weak;
translations.idiomatic: states with incomplete constitutions, such as Turkey and Egypt, have declined;

sentences.zh: 有憲法不平允之國，如俄羅斯則擾亂無已時矣。

translations.literal: there are states with constitutions that are not equitable, as Russia, which knows unceasing disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: and states with constitutions that are not fairly applied, such as Russia, suffer unrest without end.

sentences.zh: 種因既殊，結果亦異。

translations.literal: The causes being different, the results are also different.
translations.idiomatic: Different causes yield different outcomes.

sentences.zh: 故有雖革改而適以召亂者，此政體之不同也。

translations.literal: Hence there are cases where, though one reforms, one precisely summons disorder—this is the difference in forms of polity.
translations.idiomatic: Hence some reforms only invite chaos—such is the difference among political systems.

sentences.zh: 覘其國力，陸軍之強莫如德，海軍之強莫如英，國民之富莫如美，此國力之不同也。

translations.literal: Observing national strength: in army strength none equals Germany; in naval strength none equals Britain; in national wealth none equals America—this is the difference in national power.
translations.idiomatic: Measured by national power, Germany leads in land forces, Britain in sea power, and America in popular wealth—such are the differences in strength among nations.

sentences.zh: 窺其政略，則俄、法同盟，英、日同盟，德、奧、義同盟，既互相倚助以求國勢之穩固；

translations.literal: Peering at state policy: Russia and France ally, Britain and Japan ally, Germany, Austria, and Italy ally—each mutually relying to seek the securing of national power;
translations.idiomatic: In foreign policy, Russia and France are allied, as are Britain and Japan, and Germany, Austria, and Italy—each bloc leaning on partners to steady its national position;

sentences.zh: 德、法摩洛哥之會議，英、俄東亞之協商，其對於中國者，德、美海軍之擴張，美、法屯軍之增額，又各審利害以為商業之競爭。

translations.literal: the German-French conference at Morocco, the British-Russian consultations in East Asia; regarding China—the expansion of German and American navies, the increase of American and French garrison troops—each again weighs advantage and harm for commercial competition.
translations.idiomatic: the German-French conference over Morocco, Anglo-Russian talks on East Asia; toward China—the expansion of German and American fleets, increases in American and French garrisons—each power weighs gain and loss in commercial rivalry.

sentences.zh: 蓋列強對峙之中，無有一國孤立可以圖存者，勢使然也。

translations.literal: For among the great powers confronting one another, not one state isolated can scheme survival—the trend compels it.
translations.idiomatic: Among rival great powers, no nation can survive in isolation; circumstance demands alliances.

sentences.zh: 況人民生殖日繁，智識日開，內力亦愈以澎漲。

translations.literal: Moreover the people's propagation grows daily more numerous, knowledge daily more open, and internal strength daily more surging.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover populations multiply, learning spreads, and domestic energies swell ever faster.

sentences.zh: 故各國政策，或因殖民而造西伯利亞之鐵路，或因​​商務而開巴拿馬之運河，或因國富而投資本於世界，均有深意存焉。

translations.literal: Hence the policies of the various states—some build the Siberian railway for colonization, some open the Panama canal for commerce, some invest capital throughout the world for national wealth—all harbor deep intent.
translations.idiomatic: Hence national policies—building the Trans-Siberian Railway for colonization, opening the Panama Canal for trade, or investing capital worldwide to grow national wealth—all serve deliberate strategic ends.

sentences.zh: 此政略之不同也。

translations.literal: This is the difference in state policy.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the differences in strategic policy.

sentences.zh: 驗其民氣，俄民志偉大而少秩序，其國失之無教；

translations.literal: Testing the people's temper: Russians have lofty ambition but little order—their state fails through lack of instruction;
translations.idiomatic: Judging national character, Russians are ambitious but disorderly—their state suffers from poor civic education;

sentences.zh: 法民好美術而流晏逸，其國失之過奢；

translations.literal: the French love fine arts and drift into ease and indulgence—their state fails through excess of luxury;
translations.idiomatic: the French love art and leisure and their state suffers from extravagance;

sentences.zh: 德民性倔強而尚武勇，其國失之太驕；

translations.literal: the Germans are stubborn by nature and esteem martial valor—their state fails through too much pride;
translations.idiomatic: the Germans are stubborn and martial and their state suffers from overweening pride;

sentences.zh: 美民喜自由而多放任，其國失之複雜；

translations.literal: the Americans delight in liberty and are much given to indulgence—their state fails through complexity;
translations.idiomatic: Americans prize liberty and lax discipline and their state suffers from complexity;

sentences.zh: 義民尚功利而近貪詐，其國失之困貧；

translations.literal: the Italians esteem utility and profit and approach greed and deceit—their state fails through impoverishment;
translations.idiomatic: Italians chase profit and border on greed and deceit and their state remains poor;

sentences.zh: 惟英人富於自治自營之精神，有獨立不羈之氣象，人格之高，風俗之厚，為各國所不及。

translations.literal: Only the English are rich in the spirit of self-government and self-reliance, possess an air of independent unconstrained character, elevation of person, thickness of custom—beyond what the various states can reach.
translations.idiomatic: Only the English possess a spirit of self-government and self-reliance, an independent bearing, high personal character, and sturdy customs unmatched elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 此民氣之不同也。

translations.literal: This is the difference in popular temper.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the differences in national character.

sentences.zh: 臣等觀於各國之大勢既如此，又參綜比較，窮其得失之源，實不外君臣一心，上下相維，然後可收舉國一致之益。

translations.literal: We your ministers, observing the great trends of the various states to be thus, and again synthesizing comparisons to exhaust the sources of gain and loss, find it in fact not outside ruler and ministers of one mind, superior and inferior mutually sustaining—only then can one harvest the benefit of the whole state's unanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Having surveyed these world trends and weighed them together, we find the root of success or failure lies in unity between ruler and ministers and mutual support between court and country—only then can the whole nation move as one.

sentences.zh: 否則，名實相懸，有可以斷其無效者，約有三端：一曰，無開誠之心者國必危。

translations.literal: Otherwise, name and reality hang apart; there are roughly three points by which one may conclude ineffectiveness: first, those without a heart of openness and sincerity—the state must be imperiled.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise name and reality diverge, and three signs mark failure: first, states that lack sincerity court ruin.

sentences.zh: 西班牙苛待殖民，致有斐律賓、古巴之敗。

translations.literal: Spain harshly treated colonies, bringing defeat in the Philippines and Cuba.
translations.idiomatic: Spain oppressed its colonies and lost the Philippines and Cuba.

sentences.zh: 英鑑於美民反抗，而於澳洲、坎拿大兩域予人民以自治之權，致有今日之強盛，開誠故也。

translations.literal: Britain, taking warning from American popular resistance, in Australia and Canada gave the people powers of self-government, achieving today's strength—because of openness hence.
translations.idiomatic: Britain, learning from American rebellion, granted self-government in Australia and Canada and thereby grew strong—through sincerity.

sentences.zh: 俄滅波蘭而用嚴法以禁其語言，今揭竿而起要求權利者，即波蘭人也。

translations.literal: Russia extinguished Poland and used severe laws to forbid its language; now those rising with poles demanding rights are Poles.
translations.idiomatic: Russia destroyed Poland and banned its language; those who now rise in arms demanding rights are Poles.

sentences.zh: 又於興學練兵，皆以專制為目的，今滿洲之役，不戰先潰。

translations.literal: Again in promoting schools and training troops, all took autocracy as aim; now in the Manchurian war, before battle they collapsed first.
translations.idiomatic: Its schools and armies too served autocracy alone; in the war in Manchuria Russian forces collapsed before fighting began.

sentences.zh: 莫斯科、聖彼得堡之暴動，即出於軍人與學生也。

translations.literal: The disturbances at Moscow and Saint Petersburg issued precisely from soldiers and students.
translations.idiomatic: The uprisings in Moscow and Saint Petersburg came from soldiers and students.

sentences.zh: 防之愈密，而禍即伏於所防之中，患更發於所防之外，不開誠故也。

translations.literal: The more closely one guards, the more disaster lurks within what is guarded; calamity erupts further outside what is guarded—because of not being open hence.
translations.idiomatic: The tighter the guard, the deeper the danger within; trouble breaks out beyond the wall—because sincerity was lacking.

sentences.zh: 二曰，無慮遠之識者國必弱。

translations.literal: Second, those without far-seeing knowledge—the state must be weak.
translations.idiomatic: Second, states that lack foresight grow weak.

sentences.zh: 俄以交通之不便，而用中央集權，故其地方之自治，日以不整。

translations.literal: Russia, because transport is inconvenient, uses centralized power, hence local self-government daily grows less orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Russia, hampered by poor communications, relies on centralization, and local self-government steadily decays.

sentences.zh: 美以疆域之大，而用地方分權，故其中央與地方之機關，同時進步。

translations.literal: America, because its territory is large, uses distributed local power, hence central and local organs advance together.
translations.idiomatic: America, vast in territory, practices local autonomy, and both central and local institutions advance together.

sentences.zh: 治大國與治小國固不侔也。

translations.literal: Governing a great state and governing a small state are indeed not comparable.
translations.idiomatic: Governing a great empire and governing a small state are not the same task.

sentences.zh: 德以日爾曼法系趨於地方分權，雖為君主之國，而人民有參與政治之資格。

translations.literal: Germany, because the Germanic legal system trends toward local distribution of power, though a monarchical state, its people have qualification to participate in politics.
translations.idiomatic: Germany's Germanic legal tradition favors local autonomy; though a monarchy, its people participate in politics.

sentences.zh: 法以羅馬法系趨於中央集權，雖為民主之國，而政務操之官吏之手，人民反無自治之能力。

translations.literal: France, because the Roman legal system trends toward central concentration, though a democratic state, government affairs are wielded in officials' hands and the people conversely lack capacity for self-government.
translations.idiomatic: France's Roman legal tradition drives centralization; though called a democracy, officials hold real power and the people lack habits of self-rule.

sentences.zh: 兩相比較，法弱於德，有由來矣。

translations.literal: Comparing the two, France is weaker than Germany—there is cause for it.
translations.idiomatic: Compared side by side, France is weaker than Germany—and for good reason.

sentences.zh: 三曰，無同化之力者國必擾。

translations.literal: Third, those without power of assimilation—the state must be disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Third, states that cannot assimilate their peoples fall into disorder.

sentences.zh: 美以共和政體，重視人民權利，雖人種複雜，而同化力甚強，故能上下相安於無事。

translations.literal: America, with republican polity, values people's rights; though races are complex, assimilative power is very strong, hence able to have superior and inferior at peace without incident.
translations.idiomatic: America's republic honors popular rights; though its population is diverse, its assimilative power is strong, and court and country live in peace.

sentences.zh: 土耳其一國之中，分十數種族，語言宗教各不相同，又無統一之機關，致有今日之衰弱。

translations.literal: Within Turkey one state divides into a dozen-odd races; languages and religions differ and there is no unifying organ, bringing today's weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Turkey harbors a dozen peoples with different languages and faiths and no unifying institutions, and has therefore weakened.

sentences.zh: 俄則種族尤雜，不下百數，語言亦分四十餘種，其政府又多歧視之意見，致有今日之紛亂。

translations.literal: Russia's races are especially mixed, not fewer than a hundred; languages too divide into forty-odd kinds, and its government moreover holds many discriminatory views, bringing today's disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Russia's peoples are still more numerous—nearly a hundred groups and forty-odd languages—and official prejudice fuels today's turmoil.

sentences.zh: 奧、匈兩國雖同戴一君主，而兩族之容貌、習尚、語言、性情迥殊，故時起事端，將來恐不免分離之患。

translations.literal: Austria and Hungary, though both wear one monarch, the two peoples' appearance, customs, language, disposition are utterly different, hence incidents arise from time to time; the future fears separation's calamity cannot be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Austria and Hungary share one sovereign yet differ in appearance, custom, language, and temperament; disputes arise often, and separation may lie ahead.

sentences.zh: 蓋法制不一，畛域不化，顯然標其名為兩種族之國，未有能享和平、臻富強者矣。

translations.literal: For when laws and systems are not one, boundaries are not assimilated, clearly marking the name as a state of two races—never has one been able to enjoy peace and reach wealth and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Where laws diverge and peoples are not fused, a state plainly remains two nations in one—and such states never enjoy lasting peace or true strength.

sentences.zh: 此考察各國所得之實在情形也。

translations.literal: This is the actual situation obtained from investigating the various states.
translations.idiomatic: Such is what our investigation of foreign states has found.

sentences.zh: 竊惟學問以相摩而益善，國勢以相競而益強。

translations.literal: We venture to consider: learning by mutual rubbing grows better; national power by mutual rivalry grows stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Learning improves through exchange, and national strength grows through competition.

sentences.zh: 中國地處亞東，又為數千年文化之古國，不免挾尊己卑人之見，未嘗取世界列國之變遷而比較之。

translations.literal: China sits in East Asia, again an ancient state of several thousand years' culture, and cannot but carry the view of honoring self and belittling others, never taking the transformations of the world's various states to compare.
translations.idiomatic: China lies in East Asia and boasts millennia of civilization, yet tends to esteem itself and slight others, and has not measured itself against the changing powers of the world.

sentences.zh: 甲午以前，南北洋海陸軍製造各廠同時而興，聲勢一振。

translations.literal: Before the Jiawu year, the Nanyang and Beiyang naval and military manufacturing establishments all arose together and prestige was once stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Sino-Japanese War of 1894–95, Beiyang and Nanyang arsenals and shipyards rose together and China's prestige seemed to revive.

sentences.zh: 例之各省，差佔優勝矣。

translations.literal: Compared with the provinces, it somewhat held the advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with the provinces alone, it seemed ahead.

sentences.zh: 然未嘗取列國之情狀而比較之也。

translations.literal: Yet never took the various states' conditions to compare.
translations.idiomatic: Yet it was never weighed against the condition of other nations.

sentences.zh: 故比較對於內，則滿盈自阻之心日長；

translations.literal: Hence comparison directed inward daily lengthens the heart of fullness that blocks itself;
translations.idiomatic: Comparing only within breeds complacency;

sentences.zh: 比較對於外，則爭存進取之志益堅。

translations.literal: comparison directed outward daily strengthens the will to struggle for survival and advance.
translations.idiomatic: comparing outward sharpens the will to survive and advance.

sentences.zh: 然則謀國者亦善用其比較而已。」

translations.literal: Thus those who scheme for the state also need only skillfully use comparison."
translations.idiomatic: Those who plan for the nation must therefore use comparison wisely."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「臣等曠觀世界大勢，深察中國近情，非定國是，無以安大計。

translations.literal: Again they memorialized: "We your ministers broadly observe the world's great trend and deeply examine China's recent condition; without fixing the national essence, there is no means to settle the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: They submitted another memorial: "Surveying the world's great trends and China's present condition, we find that without fixing the nation's fundamental policy, no great plan can succeed.

sentences.zh: 國是之要，約有六事：一曰舉國臣民立於同等法制之下，以破除一切畛域；

translations.literal: The essentials of the national essence, roughly six matters: first, the whole nation's ministers and people stand under an equal legal system to break all boundaries;
translations.idiomatic: The essentials of national policy are roughly six: first, place all subjects under equal law to abolish every privilege and barrier;

sentences.zh: 二曰國是採決於公論；

translations.literal: second, the national essence is decided by public discussion;
translations.idiomatic: second, let national policy be decided by public deliberation;

sentences.zh: 三曰集中外之所長，以謀國家與人民之安全發達；

translations.literal: third, concentrate Chinese and foreign strengths to scheme the state and people's secure development;
translations.idiomatic: third, combine Chinese and foreign strengths to secure the nation's safety and the people's welfare;

sentences.zh: 四曰明宮府之體制；

translations.literal: fourth, clarify palace and government's system;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, clarify the institutions of court and government;

sentences.zh: 五曰定中央與地方之權限；

translations.literal: fifth, fix central and local authority limits;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, define the powers of central and local authorities;

sentences.zh: 六曰公佈國用及諸政務。

translations.literal: sixth, publicly announce state revenue and all government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: sixth, publish state finances and all major government business.

sentences.zh: 以上六事，擬請明降諭旨，宣示天下以定國是，約於十五年或二十年頒布憲法，召集國會，實行一切立憲制度。」

translations.literal: The above six matters, we propose requesting a clear imperial edict proclaiming to the realm to fix the national essence, roughly in fifteen or twenty years to promulgate a constitution, convene a national assembly, and practice all constitutional systems."
translations.idiomatic: We propose that Your Majesty issue a clear edict proclaiming these six points to the empire, and pledge to promulgate a constitution and convene a parliament in about fifteen or twenty years, putting constitutional government fully into practice."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「實行立憲，既請明定期限，則此十數年間，苟不先籌預備，轉瞬屆期，必至茫無所措。

translations.literal: Again they memorialized: "To practice constitutionalism, having already requested a clear fixed term, in these dozen-odd years if one does not first plan and prepare, in a twinkling when the term arrives one must reach confused with no measures.
translations.idiomatic: They added: "Once a deadline for constitutional rule is set, these dozen years must be used for preparation; otherwise, when the day arrives, the court will be left helpless.

sentences.zh: 今欲廓清積弊，明定責成，必先從官制入手。

translations.literal: Now wishing to sweep clear accumulated abuses and clearly fix responsibility, one must first begin from the official system.
translations.idiomatic: To clear accumulated abuses and fix clear lines of responsibility, reform must begin with the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 擬請參酌中外，統籌大局，改定全國官制，為立憲之預備。」

translations.literal: We propose requesting reference to Chinese and foreign models, overall planning of the great situation, reforming the whole nation's official system, as preparation for constitutionalism."
translations.idiomatic: We propose drawing on Chinese and foreign models to reshape the national bureaucracy as preparation for constitutional government."

sentences.zh: 均奉俞旨採納，遂定立憲之議。

translations.literal: All received imperial assent and adoption, and constitutionalism was fixed as policy.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved all these proposals, and constitutional reform became settled policy.

sentences.zh: 先是鴻慈奉使在途，已擢禮部尚書；

translations.literal: Earlier, while Hongci was on the mission abroad, he had already been elevated Minister of Rites;
translations.idiomatic: While Hongci was still abroad on the mission, he had already been promoted Minister of Rites;

sentences.zh: 及還，充釐定官制大臣，轉法部尚書。

translations.literal: on return he was appointed Deliberation on the Official System Grand Minister, then transferred Minister of Law.
translations.idiomatic: on his return he served as commissioner for revising the bureaucracy, then became Minister of Law.

sentences.zh: 充經筵講官、參預政務大臣。

translations.literal: He served as Classics Lecturer and Grand Minister for Participating in Government Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as lecturer at the imperial lectures and as a minister participating in government affairs.

sentences.zh: 時法部初設，與大理院畫分權責，往復爭議，又改並部中職掌。

translations.literal: At the time the Ministry of Law was newly established; with the Supreme Court of Justice demarcating authority and duty, back-and-forth dispute, and again reformed merged duties within the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Law had just been created; he demarcated powers with the Supreme Court amid repeated disputes and reorganized the ministry's functions.

sentences.zh: 於是京外各級審判廳次第設矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon trial courts at each level in capital and provinces were set up in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Trial courts at every level were then established in the capital and provinces.

sentences.zh: 又採英、美製創立京師模範監獄。

translations.literal: Again adopting British and American systems, he established the capital model prison.
translations.idiomatic: He also founded a model prison in the capital on British and American lines.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，疾作，乞解職，溫旨慰留。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year illness arose; he begged release from office; a warm edict comforted and detained him.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 34 he fell ill, asked to resign, and received a gracious edict urging him to remain.

sentences.zh: 兩宮升遐，力疾視事。

translations.literal: When the two palaces ascended to the beyond, he forced himself through illness to attend to duties.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager and Emperor died, he forced himself to continue his duties despite illness.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，賞一等第三寶星，充報聘俄國專使大臣​​。

translations.literal: In Xuantong first year he was rewarded the First Class Third Grade Precious Star and appointed envoy extraordinary on return visit to Russia.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 1 he received the First Class Third Grade Precious Star and served as envoy on a return mission to Russia.

sentences.zh: 禮成返國，奏言：「道經東三省，目擊日、俄二國之經營殖民地不遺餘力。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed he returned to the country and memorialized: "Passing through the Three Eastern Provinces, witnessing Japan and Russia's two states' management of colonies without sparing effort.
translations.idiomatic: After completing his mission he returned and memorialized: "Traveling through the Three Eastern Provinces, I saw Japan and Russia devoting every effort to colonization.

sentences.zh: 非急籌抵制，無以固邊圉；

translations.literal: Unless urgently planning countermeasures, there is no means to secure the border;
translations.idiomatic: Unless countermeasures are planned at once, the frontier cannot be held;

sentences.zh: 非振興實業擴其自然之利，無以圖富強。

translations.literal: Unless reviving industry to expand natural advantages, there is no means to scheme wealth and strength.
translations.idiomatic: unless industry is developed to exploit natural resources, wealth and strength cannot be achieved.

sentences.zh: 請速辦墾殖、森林二端。

translations.literal: We request quickly to handle colonization and forestry two points.
translations.idiomatic: I urge immediate progress on land reclamation and forestry.

sentences.zh: 俟財力稍裕，再籌興學、路礦、兵屯各事，以資捍衛。」

translations.literal: Awaiting finances somewhat ample, again plan schools, railways, mines, military colonies each matter, to supply defense."
translations.idiomatic: When funds allow, schools, railways, mines, and military colonies should follow to strengthen defense."

sentences.zh: 臚陳辦法。

translations.literal: He detailed the methods item by item.
translations.idiomatic: He then set out his proposals in detail.

sentences.zh: 得旨，下所司議行。

translations.literal: He received the directive; it was sent down to responsible offices for deliberation and execution.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved and referred the matter to the relevant offices for implementation.

sentences.zh: 是年八月，命入軍機，晉協辦大學士。

translations.literal: That year in the eighth month he was ordered into the Grand Council and promoted Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of that year he entered the Grand Council and was promoted Associate Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 二年，卒，加太子少保，諡文誠。

translations.literal: In the second year he died; posthumously made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent; posthumous name Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 2 he died; he was posthumously made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 論曰：樞臣入對，序次有定，後列者非特詢不得越言。

translations.literal: The discussion states: Grand Council ministers entering audience have fixed order of precedence; those later in rank may not by special inquiry overstep to speak.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: When Grand Council ministers attended audience, precedence was fixed; junior members could not speak out of turn even when questioned.

sentences.zh: 晚近領以尊親，勢尤禁隔，旅進旅退而已。

translations.literal: In recent times led by honored kin, influence was especially forbidden and separate, merely advancing and retreating in cohorts.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times princes led the council, power was still more fenced off, and ministers merely advanced and withdrew in company.

sentences.zh: 景廉多戰績，額勒和布有清操，庚身、應溥通達諸諳練，壽恆有責難之言，鴻慈負知新之譽，榮慶謹慎持躬，那桐和敏解事，皆庶幾大臣之選者歟？

translations.literal: Jing Lian had many battle achievements, E Lei He Bu had pure integrity, Gengshen and Yingpu were thoroughly practiced in all affairs, Shouheng had words of reproach, Hongci bore repute for knowing what is new, Rong Qing was careful in personal conduct, Na Tong was harmonious and quick to resolve affairs—all perhaps nearly choices for great ministers, are they not?
translations.idiomatic: Jing Lian won many battles, E Lei He Bu kept a clean reputation, Gengshen and Yingpu were seasoned in every branch of government, Shouheng spoke with sharp criticism, Hongci earned fame for embracing reform, Rong Qing was careful in conduct, and Na Tong was tactful and capable—were they not all, in their way, fit to rank among the great ministers of the age?
